clue.text: Chapter is rejected, containing stuff that's tasteless, not moving

indicators.note: containing means the turned piece holds the other piece within it
rejected means sent back, so the chapter-plus-is piece is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
tat is cheap, tasteless goods or ornaments

explanation.surface: A dull, tasteless chapter is turned down by a publisher for going nowhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not moving' looks like part of the tasteless stuff's description, but it is the definition; 'rejected' turns only the chapter and 'is', which 'containing' then wraps round the tat.
explanation.definitionFit: Something static stays put, without any motion.

clue.text: Ceremony after time lacking novelty

indicators.note: after places the ceremony behind the time letter in the answer

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony

explanation.surface: A ceremony held out of habit has lost any freshness.
explanation.definitionFit: Trite remarks are stale and overused, so they have no freshness.

clue.text: Engine, right inside boat, expert put into operation

indicators.note: inside means the letter for right sits within the word for boat

parts.note: a tub is a slow, clumsy boat

indicators.note: put into means the expert goes within the abbreviation for operation

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert

explanation.surface: An expert mechanic gets an engine running inside a boat.
explanation.definitionFit: A turboprop is a jet engine driving a propeller, a type of aircraft engine.

clue.text: Managing top course

definitions.meaning: the top layer of masonry on a wall, often sloping

explanation.surface: Someone handling the top layer of brickwork.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting by is managing; and the capping layer of brick or stone on a wall shares the same name.

clue.text: Loss of confidence about previous achievement voiced

parts.note: C is short for circa, Latin for about

indicators.note: voiced means the phrase for a past achievement is heard said out loud

parts.note: an old feat is a past achievement

explanation.surface: Someone losing nerve recalls an earlier success.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa) comes first; then 'old feat' said out loud sounds like 'old feet'.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting cold feet is the idiom for losing nerve before a big step.

clue.text: Game with variety of rich sequences by which man's enthralled

indicators.note: enthralled means held captive, so the rearranged letters hold the word for man
a variety of the letters means they are mixed up into a new order

parts.note: he stands for a man

explanation.surface: A game full of rich sequences in which a player becomes captivated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variety of' rearranges RICH SEQUENCES, and 'enthralled' puts HE inside that mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Chinese chequers is a board game of hopping marbles across a star.

clue.text: Artist gets poetic continually

parts.note: lands means gets, as in lands a job
e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning continually

explanation.surface: An artist keeps on producing poetry.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Edwin Landseer was a Victorian painter of animals, who also made the lions in Trafalgar Square, London.
explanation.definitionFit: Landseer was a celebrated English painter, the Monarch of the Glen being his best-known picture.

clue.text: Dirt from yacht lifted up

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom
from means the letters are taken out of the run of words

explanation.surface: Grime is hauled up out of a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' points to the run yacHT LIFted; 'up' turns HTLIF into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Filth is foul dirt or grime.

clue.text: Politician engaged in revision of cases on hold

indicators.note: engaged in means the politician sits within the reworked letters
a revision of the letters reworks them into a new order

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An MP busy revising case files that have been put on hold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'revision of' rearranges CASES ON, and 'engaged in' puts MP inside: ENCO-MP-ASS.
explanation.definitionFit: To encompass is to contain or include, much as to hold does.

clue.text: Row about increase in wild riots and upheaval

indicators.note: about means the word for row goes around everything else

parts.note: a din is a noisy row

indicators.note: in means the word for increase goes within the rearranged letters
wild means the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: to up something is to increase it

explanation.surface: A noisy row and rising tension in violent riots cause chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a line or a verb; here it is a noisy quarrel. 'wild' mixes the riots, 'in' sets the increase inside them, and 'about' wraps the row round everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Disruption is disorder and turmoil, the same as an upheaval.

clue.text: See officer in command getting mad

indicators.note: 'getting' puts one piece inside the other

parts.note: lo is an old word for look or see
OC stands for officer commanding

explanation.surface: Watch the commanding officer losing his mind.
explanation.definitionFit: Loco is slang for crazy.

clue.text: Express disapproval of animal's habitation

parts.note: a den is an animal's lair or dwelling
an ounce is a big cat, the snow leopard

explanation.surface: Condemn the place where a beast lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The ounce is another name for the snow leopard. The possessive is read as 'den of ounce', so the habitation comes first in the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To denounce is to condemn publicly, to speak out against.

clue.text: Arrangement that's made finally to defend border

indicators.note: to defend means the outer letters guard the word for border on both sides

parts.note: sc., short for scilicet, means that is or namely

indicators.note: finally picks out the final letter of the word made

parts.note: a hem is the border of a garment

explanation.surface: A deal is finally struck to protect a frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' stands for sc., short for Latin scilicet ('namely'), a convention worth knowing; 'finally' takes the last of 'made', and 'to defend' sets the border inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A scheme is a plan or system for organising things.

clue.text: Engage in argument in yard

definitions.meaning: to quarrel or dispute, like boxers trading blows
a yard on a ship is a pole holding a sail

explanation.surface: Two people quarrelling in the back garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yard' here is the nautical yard, a ship's pole, not a garden.
explanation.definitionFit: To dispute is to box verbally; and a ship's mast or boom is the same word.

clue.text: Early work of image-maker 'unoriginal — no thanks'

parts.note: PR, public relations, crafts a public image

indicators.note: no means the word for thanks is left out

parts.note: imitative work copies others, so is unoriginal
ta is British slang for thanks

explanation.surface: A critic dismisses an image-maker's first piece as derivative.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes the slang for thanks out of the word for unoriginal; 'work of' only joins the definition to the wordplay. Ta is British slang for thank you.
explanation.definitionFit: Primitive means belonging to the earliest stage of development.

clue.text: River with reflected sheep keeping place in illustration

parts.note: the Exe is a river in Devon

indicators.note: keeping means the turned word holds the abbreviation for place
reflected means the word for sheep is seen backwards, as in a mirror

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

explanation.surface: A river mirrors a sheep at a beauty spot, a perfect picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The Exe is a river in Devon, England. 'reflected' turns the sheep backwards, and 'keeping' has it hold the place abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a model or typical example used to illustrate.

clue.text: Chaplain nearly broken by cold king with wicked punishment

indicators.note: broken by means the shortened chaplain is split open by the next letters
nearly means the last letter of the chaplain is lopped off

parts.note: a padre is a military chaplain
K is the chess abbreviation for king
ill can mean evil or wicked, as in ill deeds

explanation.surface: An army chaplain is shattered by a cold-hearted king's cruel sentence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nearly' leaves PADR; 'broken by' puts CK into it as PA-CK-DR, and ILL follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Pack drill was a military penalty of marching in full kit.

clue.text: Bar restricting material allowed on flight

definitions.text: Bar restricting material allowed on flight

parts.words: Bar restricting material allowed on flight
parts.note: reads like a ban on luggage for air travel; it is really a metal rod holding carpet in place on a staircase

explanation.walkthrough: 'flight' is a flight of stairs, not an air journey, and the 'material' is the carpet.
explanation.definitionFit: A stair rod runs across the back of each step to keep the runner of carpet in place.

clue.text: Quarrel in police department brought about by hard report

indicators.note: in means the quarrel sits within the turned abbreviation
brought about means turned round, so the police department letters are read backwards

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of British police
a spat is a petty quarrel
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: A row in the police department is triggered by a tough report.
explanation.walkthrough: CID is the detective branch of British police. 'brought about' turns it round, 'in' lodges the quarrel inside, and the hard pencil grade ends the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispatch is an official report, as from a war correspondent.

clue.text: Prize squad's leader divides, making a point

indicators.note: divides means the letter splits the trophy word in two

parts.note: a cup is a trophy or prize

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of squad's

explanation.surface: A team captain splits the trophy money to make a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A cusp is a pointed end, as of a tooth or a crescent moon.

clue.text: Love being in touch with one with southern dialect

parts.note: a pat is a light touch
love is zero, O, in tennis scores
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A lover keeps in touch with someone who speaks with a southern accent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'being in' and 'with' are link words joining PAT, O, I and S in order.
explanation.definitionFit: A patois is a local or regional dialect.

clue.text: Desire to follow end of meal with one fruit

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word meal

parts.note: an itch is a craving or desire
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Craving a single piece of fruit at the end of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to follow' puts ITCH after L, the end of 'meal'.
explanation.definitionFit: The litchi, or lychee, is a sweet Chinese fruit.

clue.text: Cruel, without regret, plan allegation

indicators.note: without means the letters for regret are taken out

parts.note: to rue is to regret
an aim is a plan or intention

explanation.surface: A cruel, remorseless scheme behind an accusation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' takes the regret out of the cruel; the plan follows to finish.
explanation.definitionFit: A claim is an assertion that something is true, like an allegation.

clue.text: Problem presented by rook in time, as by knight earlier on

parts.note: qua is Latin for as, in the capacity of
N is the chess notation for knight

indicators.note: in means the rook sits within the word for time

parts.note: a day is a period of time
R is the chess abbreviation for rook

explanation.surface: A chess dilemma: a rook moves in time, with a knight played earlier.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess words mislead: only rook and knight are notation letters. 'earlier on' puts the Latin 'as' and the knight before the rook-in-time piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A quandary is a dilemma, a state of perplexity.

clue.text: Bring up mass to get ready to fight again

parts.note: to rear is to bring up, as with children

explanation.surface: Raising a mass of troops to return to battle.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to equip with weapons once more.

clue.text: Beckham, opening out, going around with singer

indicators.note: going around means the shortened name is read backwards
opening out means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: David Beckham, the English footballer

explanation.surface: A footballer opens up and goes out with a pop star.
explanation.walkthrough: 'opening out' drops D from DAVID to give AVID; 'going around' turns that into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A diva is a leading female opera singer.

clue.text: Silly chortle with air that's insincere

indicators.note: silly means the letters are put into a foolish new order

explanation.surface: A giggling remark made with a false air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silly' rearranges CHORTLE + AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rhetorical gesture is made for show, without sincere meaning.

clue.text: Barmaid used to work without assistance serving shorts

indicators.note: to work means the letters are reworked, and without means some of them are left out

parts.note: aid is assistance

explanation.surface: A barmaid used to serve alone, wearing shorts.
explanation.walkthrough: BARMAID USED, less AID, rearranges into the answer: Bermuda shorts reach to just above the knee.
explanation.definitionFit: Bermudas are knee-length shorts named after the islands.

clue.text: Single male not initially serious

parts.note: sole means only or single

indicators.note: initially takes the first letters of male and not

explanation.surface: A lone man who is not initially in earnest.
explanation.definitionFit: Solemn means grave and earnest.
